setup: Loop a mini band around your legs just above your knees, or around your ankles for greater resistance.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart so that the band is under constant tension.
Hinge slightly at the hips and bend your knees into a stable quarter-squat position with your chest lifted and core braced.
steps: Take a short diagonal step forward and outward with one foot, driving out against the band without letting the knee collapse inward.
Plant the foot firmly, maintaining hip-width distance or wider between your feet.
Step the opposite foot forward and outward in the opposite diagonal direction to match, continuing the zig-zag pattern.
After completing the prescribed steps forward, reverse the direction by stepping backward and outward while maintaining continuous band tension.
instructions.breathing: Breathe continuously and smoothly throughout the walk, bracing your core with each step.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the knees to cave inward into valgus collapse.
common_faults.correction: Actively push your knees outward against the band so they remain stacked over your middle toes.

common_faults.fault: Standing up straight and losing the athletic quarter-squat posture.
common_faults.correction: Keep your hips and knees loaded in a shallow squat position throughout the entire set.

common_faults.fault: Bringing the feet too close together between steps, causing the band to go slack.
common_faults.correction: Maintain at least hip-width separation at all times so tension on the hip abductors is never lost.

precautions: Ensure the floor path is completely clear of obstacles, especially when performing the backward stepping phase.

name: Banded Monster Walk
summary: A dynamic hip-abductor and glute strengthening exercise performed by walking diagonally against resistance band tension in a quarter-squat stance.
